title: Degreewise exchange compatibility with a morphism of squares and coefficients
statement:
Let $X_0,Y_0,S_0,T_0,X_1,Y_1,S_1,T_1$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $h_b:Y_b\to X_b$, $e_b:Y_b\to T_b$, $f_b:X_b\to S_b$, $g_b:T_b\to S_b$ for $b=0,1$, satisfying $f_bh_b=g_be_b$. Give morphisms $x:X_1\to X_0$, $y:Y_1\to Y_0$, $s:S_1\to S_0$, $a:T_1\to T_0$ satisfying $f_0x=sf_1$, $g_0a=sg_1$, $h_0y=xh_1$, and $e_0y=ae_1$.
Suppose the two squares $f_bh_b=g_be_b$ are cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]; the comparison faces need only commute. Let $F_0$ and $F_1$ be abelian sheaves on $(T_0)_{\Et}$ and $(T_1)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $\phi:a^{-1}F_0\to F_1$ be any morphism, and let $q\geq0$. For any commutative face use the degree-$q$ exchange obtained from the bounded below derived mate [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange] applied to the coefficient sheaf in degree zero, using the natural exact-inverse-image cohomology identifications [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Higher direct images mean $R^qu_*G=\mathcal H^q(Ru_*G[0])$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $P^q_{F_0}:s^{-1}R^qg_{0,*}F_0\to R^qg_{1,*}a^{-1}F_0$ and $Q^q_{e_0^{-1}F_0}:x^{-1}R^qh_{0,*}e_0^{-1}F_0\to R^qh_{1,*}y^{-1}e_0^{-1}F_0$ be the comparison-face exchanges. Let $\beta_{b,G}:f_b^{-1}R^qg_{b,*}G\to R^qh_{b,*}e_b^{-1}G$ be the usual higher-direct-image base-change map [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology]. Define
$$ U_\phi=f_1^{-1}(R^qg_{1,*}\phi)\circ f_1^{-1}P^q_{F_0}:x^{-1}f_0^{-1}R^qg_{0,*}F_0\longrightarrow f_1^{-1}R^qg_{1,*}F_1, $$
$$ V_\phi=R^qh_{1,*}(e_1^{-1}\phi)\circ R^qh_{1,*}(\chi_{F_0})\circ Q^q_{e_0^{-1}F_0}:x^{-1}R^qh_{0,*}e_0^{-1}F_0\longrightarrow R^qh_{1,*}e_1^{-1}F_1, $$
where $\chi:y^{-1}e_0^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_1^{-1}a^{-1}$ and the identification $x^{-1}f_0^{-1}\cong f_1^{-1}s^{-1}$ in $U_\phi$ are the canonical inverse-image composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Then
$$ \beta_{1,F_1}\circ U_\phi=V_\phi\circ x^{-1}\beta_{0,F_0}. $$
Neither $\phi$ nor the comparison-face exchanges are required to be isomorphisms. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, affineness or torsion assumption is imposed.
